data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The evidence that distinguishes 'independent' from 'merely uncorrelated' is a rigorous dependency audit proving non-overlapping supply chains, because correlation in software systems is almost always caused by shared dependencies rather than coincidental independent bugs.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A shared dependency is not the cause of a specific failure","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Operators have proprietary, non-overlapping stacks but identical external interfaces","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The correlation is caused by a shared external trigger rather than a shared internal component","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Software failures are rarely truly independent due to the high complexity of modern systems. Apparent independence is often due to shared third-party libraries, OS kernels, or hardware architectures. A decentralized network's claim of independence is only substantiated by a dependency audit proving the operators do not share common-mode dependencies. If the audit reveals overlapping supply chains (e.g., all use the same OS version), the failures are not independent, regardless of organizational separation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
